_comment: Tier-2 for sparta particle_emission and chemistry: two numbers a deck will quietly get wrong. Four decks were run on the installed binary (SPARTA 24 Sep 2025, spa_serial). particle_emission:1 — two argon decks emitting on xlo differ only by an 'nrho 4e20' keyword appended to the mixture line while 'global nrho 1e20' stays put; the steady particle count comes out 4.03 times higher, so the MIXTURE value is what sets the emitted flux, and both runs exit 0 with no error and no warning. chemistry:3 — two air TCE decks differ only in the mixture temperature. At 273 K Ncoll is in the thousands per step while Nreact is 0 on every stats line AND the N, O and NO counts are strictly 0, which is a cold deck, not a broken one. At 20000 K the product counts reach five figures and keep climbing while Nreact still reads single digits on every line, because Nreact is a PER-STEP count. So Nreact cannot distinguish the two cases and the species counts can. Every assertion is a ratio between the two decks or the presence/absence of product particles; no count is pinned. COVERS: particle_emission:1, chemistry:3.
